Steak was average and price is Fair. It’s neither cheap nor expensive.
Apr 2023 • Friends
Solid three star experience. I had a nice chat with the gentleman co-owner one day while walking on the street and was asked to come try the restaurant.

Ok. My job is literally to try restaurants, so sure, I came back the following day.

Ambience: If anything this is what I would expect from a restaurant if I was transported back to the 1970s. Lots on the menu, no particular specialty. Something for everyone.

Food: Ordered a steak and some garlic toast and everything was as expected. Average. Unrefined.

Interesting point, the co-owner partner (the wife, if I dare assume), was quite proud of the beef that they use. Apparently they import their own beef which would indicate a discerning taste for beef, then.

One odd tidbit, however, raised an eyebrow. The lady co-owner made a claim that their cattle are finished with strawberries.

The finishing period is when beef are fed an energy-dense diet so that they will grow rapidly and add muscle/meat to their frame and optimise fat cover in preparation for slaughter. Corn. Oats. Barley. And lots of it. 10-15 lbs a day.

The claim of the owners they their cattle is finished with strawberries just doesn’t seem to bear any validity. Maybe I’m wrong. I did also put this out to my Australian beef producer network (Blackmore, Stockyard, etc.) and nothing came back.

Ok let’s table that. Steak was average.

Finally pricing: Fair. It’s neither cheap nor expensive. The diner can rest assured to get decent value by dining here.

So, would I come back?

The answer is no. There’s nothing sufficiently compelling here to pull me back and a whole world of restaurants to discover.
